note: English study material for post 03, kept OUT of the blog. C1 and C2 only. Levels are AI4Read estimates in the style of the English Vocabulary Profile and English Grammar Profile, not an official grading; an independent reviewer should check them. Example sentences restate ideas from the post or state our reading, labelled where they go beyond it. Three expressions (in lockstep, to hinge on, to be tantamount to) are repeated from earlier packs for spaced review, with their headwords unchanged.

items.definition: to show that something said or believed is true

items.sentence: The idea that a reader hears only the sum squares with the toy, where attention 1 is silent to the reader (1, 2).

items.sentence: What matters for a read is not the coordinates but the dot product.
items.definition: A 'what' clause as the subject puts one idea in focus: 'What matters is …'. It works in speech and in academic writing.

items.sentence: Having added the four writes, we get the stream (4, 2).
items.definition: 'Having + past participle' shows that one action was finished before the next. The subject of the main clause must be the one who did the first action (see dangling modifiers).

items.sentence: It is essential that the additivity check be run on the model you actually use.
items.definition: After words like essential, important, insist or recommend, formal English uses the base verb ('that the check be run'), not 'is run' or 'should be run'.

items.sentence: Should the additivity check fail with the hooks placed correctly, the identity does not hold for that model.
items.definition: 'Should + subject + verb' replaces 'If the check should fail' in a formal, slightly unlikely condition. Do not add 'if'.

items.sentence: A stream with fewer dimensions than features cannot give every feature its own perpendicular direction.
items.wrong: A stream with less dimensions than features cannot give every feature its own perpendicular direction.
items.right: A stream with fewer dimensions than features cannot give every feature its own perpendicular direction.
items.definition: Use 'fewer' with countable plural nouns (dimensions, features) and 'less' with uncountable ones (less noise).

items.sentence: Adding a vector affects every score; the effect is the same shift, u dot v, for each point.
items.wrong: Adding a vector effects every score; the affect is the same shift.
items.right: Adding a vector affects every score; the effect is the same shift.
items.definition: 'Affect' is usually a verb (to change); 'effect' is usually a noun (the result). 'To effect' means to bring about, as in 'to effect a change'.

items.headword: the number of / a number of
items.sentence: The number of dimensions in GPT-2 small is 768.
items.wrong: The number of dimensions in GPT-2 small are 768.
items.right: The number of dimensions in GPT-2 small is 768.
items.definition: 'The number of …' takes a singular verb (it is about the count). 'A number of …' means 'several' and takes a plural verb.

items.sentence: Attention 1 is orthogonal to the reader (1, 2).
items.wrong: Attention 1 is orthogonal with the reader (1, 2).
items.right: Attention 1 is orthogonal to the reader (1, 2).
items.definition: Some adjectives fix their preposition: orthogonal to, independent of, equal to, similar to. 'Orthogonal with' is not used.

Shadow the loop paragraph twice, then close it and say in three sentences what the notebook bears out and what it leaves untested.

loop.text: Every part of the model adds its write to one shared list, so the residual stream is a running sum. To a first approximation, a read is then a dot product with that sum, and the norm in front of it is the part that is not linear. That much is true by construction in the toy, and the notebook bears it out on GPT-2 small, where the writes add up to the stream within rounding error. Whether the identity will hold up for other models is another matter, and results may not simply carry over to a trained Qwen3 or Llama, which we did not run. The last entry of a library's list is a case in point: it has been normalised, so to take it at face value would be a mistake. The claim that concepts are directions hinges on evidence the sources do not supply, so we are on firmer ground with the arithmetic than with the interpretation. A steering push moves every score in lockstep, yet to say that a high score shows the model uses the direction would be tantamount to confusing seeing with doing.
